resources.string: Tap the EN button to translate the screen. Tap it again to remove the English. Drag the button to move it. Scroll inside a box to read the rest. Text is read only when you tap, stays on the device, and is not saved.

An EN button stays on top of your other apps. Drag it to move it.

Tap it to cover the German on the screen with English. Scroll inside a box to read the rest. Tap the button again and the German is back.

Android cannot change the words inside other apps. The English is drawn on top.
EN button: allow display over other apps
Allow display over other apps. An orange EN button then stays on top of your other apps. Drag it to move it.

The EN button should now be on screen. Drag it to move it.\n\nTurn on accessibility so tapping that button can read the screen. If the switch is disabled, open app info, tap the three dots at the top, and allow restricted settings. Confirm with your fingerprint or face, then turn the switch on.
About 30 MB, once. After this, translation stays on the phone. Wi-Fi is the better network. Words from other apps are not uploaded and are not saved.
Android blocked the button. Allow Translate to display over other apps, then return here.
Tap the EN button to translate. Drag it to move it. Scroll inside a box to read the rest. Tap the button again to see the German.

Pictures, many games, and some banking apps do not expose their words, so those stay in German. A normal label, message, or sentence can be translated. The button does not read the screen until you tap it.
The download failed. Check the connection and try again.
Download the model in Translate first

Tap to translate this screen into English. Drag to move the button. Tap again to clear.
Tap the orange EN button to translate. Scroll a box to read the rest. Tap the button again to clear it.
